name_story.story: Shahid can be understood through the Arabic form شَاهِد, whose central sense is shahid; witness. Shahid is Arabic شَاهِد (Shāhid), the active participle of شَهِدَ, meaning 'witness'.

faq.a: Shahid is associated with the Arabic form شَاهِد, whose core sense is shahid; witness.

faq.q: What is the origin of Shahid?
faq.a: Shahid is associated with Arabic. Shahid is Arabic شَاهِد (Shāhid), the active participle of شَهِدَ, meaning 'witness'.
Yes — the underlying form شَاهِد is Arabic.
Shahid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shahid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ش ه د is Quranic (witness), but Shāhid is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shahid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Shahid is rendered شاہد and carries the sense شاہد، گواہ.

faq.q: What does Shahid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shahid is rendered شاهد and carries the sense شاهد، گواه.
A romanized syllable approximation is sha-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shahid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shahid, shahid. Script forms are شاهد, شاہد, شَاهِد, शाहिद.

faq.q: Is Shahid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
